exhibits.title: Favorite No. 20
exhibits.subtitle: J. Stevens Arms · c. 1894–1935 (Favorite family; No. 20 end date not isolated)
exhibits.summary: The smoothbore Favorite: same as the No. 17 but with a smooth barrel and no rear sight. Exists in .32 rimfire shot too, which makes it the core of our .32 honorable mention.
details: c. 1894–1935 (Favorite family; No. 20 end date not isolated)
$75–$250 (2011 Blue Book grades, 60%–100%); $150 sold (2011 Proxibid). Unverified for today's market.
sources: SASS Wire thread quoting 2001 Standard Catalog of Firearms & 2011 Blue Book (18 Jan 2012)

exhibits.title: Crack Shot No. 26½
exhibits.subtitle: J. Stevens Arms · Within No. 26 run, 1912–1939 (+1943 batch); exact 26½ years disputed
exhibits.summary: Our namesake. Stevens sold the side-lever Crack Shot from 1890 and the under-lever No. 26 from 1912; the 26½ is the same gun with a smooth bore "intended for shot cartridges." In 1902 a Crack Shot cost $2.25.
details: Within No. 26 run, 1912–1939 (+1943 batch); exact 26½ years disputed
$250 sold (iCollector, 2025). One comp only: unverified as a range. 2011 Blue Book put it about $25 under a No. 20.
sources: SASS Wire thread quoting 2001 Standard Catalog of Firearms & 2011 Blue Book (18 Jan 2012)

exhibits.title: Model 36
exhibits.subtitle: Winchester · 1920–1927
exhibits.summary: Winchester's only U.S. 9mm Flobert garden gun, roughly 20,000 made and unserialized. A cousin, not a .22, but it belongs in any shot-cartridge hall.
details: $400–$800 typical (GUNS Magazine, 2023); individual hammers to ~$1,080 reported, unverified.

exhibits.title: 41 SB Targetmaster
exhibits.subtitle: Remington · c. 1936–1939 (parent 41)
exhibits.summary: Smoothbore variant of the prewar Model 41, listed on Remington's history pages. Uncommon and thinly documented.

exhibits.title: Model 100SB
exhibits.subtitle: Marlin · 1936–1941
exhibits.summary: Barrel stamped "SMOOTH BORE – RECESS CHOKE" with a shotgun bead. Marlin collectors also mention rare 101SB and 80SB smoothbores from the 1940s (unverified).
details: .22 S/L/LR; marked "FOR 22 LONG RIFLE SHOT CTGS"
sources: Rimfire Central: Old Marlin single shot

exhibits.title: Model 67 Smoothbore / Miniature Target Bore
exhibits.subtitle: Winchester · SB from 1936 or 1937; Miniature Target Bore from 1940
exhibits.summary: The plain-Jane Winchester smoothbore. The Miniature Target Bore version is the rare one.
details: SB from 1936 or 1937; Miniature Target Bore from 1940
.22 S/L/LR shot; Miniature Target Bore: .22 LR shot
About $500 in NRA Good (American Rifleman method: +100% over a $250 67A); Miniature Target Bore est. $1,700–$2,300 (Cowan's estimate, unrealized).
sources: American Rifleman: "This Old Gun: Winchester Model 67"

exhibits.title: Model 61 "Shot Only" (Routledge, later Winchester counterbore)
exhibits.subtitle: Winchester · Routledge: 1938–1939 (~75 guns); counterbore: from ~1940
exhibits.summary: The blue chip of the Hall. Early guns used Fred Routledge's stepped bore; Winchester then made its own counterbore to avoid royalties. Look for matted receivers and "FOR SHOT ONLY."
details: $3,000–$6,000 estimates (Rock Island, 2024, restored 1939 Routledge guns); $9,222.50 sold (LSB, 1951 gun, ~97%).
sources: Westley Richards used-gun note on Routledge vs. Winchester counterbore 61s

exhibits.title: 121 Fieldmaster SB (Routledge bore)
exhibits.subtitle: Remington · Routledge shipments from Feb 1939; to 1954
exhibits.summary: The Mo-Skeet-O pump. Barrels stamped "ROUTLEDGE BORE," Mo-Skeet-O, or smoothbore. Routledge partnered with Remington on the bore.
details: $1,400–$1,650 sold, 2023–Jan 2026 (LSB, CT Firearms, Legacy Collectibles, Horst/HiBid).
sources: SouthCoastToday: "Moskeet would be a fun shooting game to resurrect" (24 Jun 2017)

exhibits.title: 510SB / 511SB / 512SB
exhibits.subtitle: Remington · 510: 1939–1962; 511: 1939–1963; 512: 1940–1962 (parent runs)
exhibits.summary: The working-class Mo-Skeet-O guns. Watch for SB, Mo-Skeet-O, or Skeetrap stamps. Easy to walk past at a gun show.
details: Bolt: single shot (510), box mag (511), tube mag (512)
No dated sold comps captured (unverified); generally below 121 SB money.
sources: Standard Catalog of Remington Firearms (2008, archive.org)

exhibits.title: 514 Routledge
exhibits.subtitle: Remington · Within 514 run, 1948–1971 (special order)
exhibits.summary: A special-order Routledge barrel on the humble 514. Gun Digest: add about $100 over a standard 514.
details: $482–$550 used/sold comps (TrueGunValue, relative dates, checked Nov 2026; unverified calendar dates).

exhibits.title: Targo: 26T, 42T, 42TR, B42T
exhibits.subtitle: O.F. Mossberg & Sons · 26T 1938–1942; 42T 1940–1942; 42TR 1940–1946 (NMCA); Targo marketed from fall 1940
exhibits.summary: Mossberg's miniature-skeet system: smoothbore bolt guns, a Model 1A barrel-mounted trap, and 2 11/16-inch birds. All bolt guns, no pumps. 26T and B42T are the scarce ones (+20%); a complete case and accessories add about 50%.
details: Bolt: single shot (26T) or box-magazine repeaters
.22 LR shot (42TR also bullets via RA-1 rifled muzzle adapter)
42T $175–$505 (Vogt sold $175, Jul 2026; asks to $505); 42TR $550 sold with trap and extensions (Apple Tree, Jun 2022).
sources: Gun Digest: "Targo! Gone But Not Forgotten"
Gun Values by Gun Digest: Targo Smoothbore Series

exhibits.title: Targo revival: 320TR, 340TR
exhibits.subtitle: O.F. Mossberg & Sons · Early 1960s (1961 NRA ".22 Shotgun Qualification Course"), dropped within ~2 years
exhibits.summary: Mossberg tried again in 1961 with NRA backing. A Mossberg VP later said breaking birds with No. 12 shot was "just too difficult and discouraging for most shooters." We think crackers fix that.
details: Early 1960s (1961 NRA ".22 Shotgun Qualification Course"), dropped within ~2 years
320TR $575 sold (Griffin & Howe listing, undated); 340TR CAD $475 sold (Kidd Family Auctions, ~Feb 2024).
sources: SSUSA: "More Than History: The National Mossberg Collectors Association"
Gun Values by Gun Digest: Targo Smoothbore Series

exhibits.title: 572SB Fieldmaster
exhibits.subtitle: Remington · 1961–1979
exhibits.summary: The last factory smoothbore pump from a big U.S. maker, until the Henry lever gun changed the game.
details: ~$750 used price point (TrueGunValue, thin data, unverified).

exhibits.title: Nylon 10 SB
exhibits.subtitle: Remington · 1962–1964
exhibits.summary: Space-age Mohawk-brown nylon meets backyard skeet. Gun Digest singles out the 24-inch SB as a small subset (forum talk: ~200 guns, unverified).
details: 19.5 in or 24 in (24 in is the rare one)

exhibits.title: 25MG Garden Gun
exhibits.subtitle: Marlin · 1999–2002
exhibits.summary: Bright front bead, no rear sight, marketed as a "Garden Gun" for snake shot.

exhibits.title: Little Badger Shotgun (and earlier RC 92)
exhibits.subtitle: Chiappa · Current
exhibits.summary: Europe's garden-gun cartridge in a folding modern package. A cousin, not a .22. The common rifled Little Badger .22 is a different gun.
sources: The Firearm Blog: The Rimfire Report, 9mm Flobert (26 Jul 2021)

exhibits.title: H1 Garden Gun (H001GG-22 / H001GG-22M)
exhibits.subtitle: Henry Repeating Arms · 2019–present
exhibits.summary: The only smoothbore .22 in current production that we know of. Capacity 14 (LR) / 11 (WMR) per Henry's spec table. Overall length 36.5 in.
sources: Henry Repeating Arms: H1 Garden Gun (fetched 11 Nov 2026)
American Rifleman: Tested: Henry Smooth Bore Garden Gun

finale.title: Honorable mention: the .32 smoothbores
finale.plaqueSub: Stevens Favorite No. 20 & Crack Shot No. 26½ in .32 rimfire shot
body: Yes, there really was a .32. What’s confirmed: Stevens catalogued its boys’-rifle smoothbores for .32 rimfire shot cartridges as well as .22. The Favorite No. 20 was “chambered for the 22 or 32 rimfire shot cartridges and has a smoothbore barrel and no rear sight” (Standard Catalog of Firearms, 2001, as quoted), and Wikipedia lists the Crack Shot No. 26½ for “.22LR Shot Cartridges, .32 Rimfire Shot Cartridges.” The gun our club is named for came in .32 shot.
Ammo: .32 rimfire shot loads existed. A Canadian collector reports shooting a No. 20 with CIL .32 Long Shot (#10, 1935-dated). That’s one collector’s report.

Likely but unverified: Remington No. 4 rolling block (a forum quote of Fjestad’s Blue Book: “the .32 smoothbore was introduced around 1911”) and No. 6 smoothbores (a forum quote of the Standard Catalog). Both are secondhand, so we’re waiting on a catalog page before calling them confirmed.
Original .32 rimfire ammunition is scarce and old. Treat these guns as display pieces unless a gunsmith says otherwise.
sources: SASS Wire, 18 Jan 2012 (Standard Catalog / Blue Book quotes)
Canadian Gun Nutz: Stevens Favorite .32 Shot
S&W Forum: Remington Model 4 in .32 rimfire
